name: Šibenik
title: Šibenik UTM: Ship Thickness Gauging in the St Anthony Channel
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Šibenik for bulk, general cargo, ferries and workboats: gauging alongside, at anchor and around the Krka estuary berths.
h1: Hull and Tank Thickness Gauging for Ships at Šibenik
intro: Šibenik stands at the head of a long, sheltered sea channel where the River Krka meets the Adriatic. Cargo ships, island ferries, tour vessels and workboats use its quays, and the deep inner bay gives owners a quiet place to wait or lay up. Atlantis NDT sends ultrasonic gauging technicians from India to the ship, whether she lies alongside, at a lay-by berth or at anchor in the bay.

highlights.p: Ships reach Šibenik through the narrow St Anthony Channel into a sheltered inner bay, where calm water makes launch transfers and careful ultrasonic readings on decks and tank tops straightforward.

highlights.h: Cargo, ferries and tour boats together
highlights.p: The port serves a small number of commercial cargo calls, island ferry routes toward Zlarin, Prvić and Kaprije, and a fleet of excursion boats for the Kornati and Krka waters.

highlights.h: Quiet waters for lay-up and waiting
highlights.p: The inner bay is used by ships awaiting orders or work elsewhere on the coast, which gives owners the time for a longer condition gauging programme than a normal port call allows.

port.h: The port of Šibenik: channel, bay and quays
p: Šibenik lies well inland of the open sea, reached by following a winding channel. Ships enter through the narrow St Anthony Channel, passing beneath a fortress on the headland, and then widen into the inner harbour and the Krka estuary beyond. This approach shelters the port from almost every sea state, and pilots are used for ships of any size. The port authority manages the commercial quays on the city side and across the bay, while the old waterfront is dominated by ferries, excursion boats and the visiting yachts that make the city a popular sailing stop.

Commercial traffic is modest but real. General cargo ships bring building materials and break-bulk goods, bulk carriers call for loose cargo, and coasters shuttle along the Adriatic. The industrial quays once supported heavier industry, and the legacy of that era remains in the form of deep-water berths, storage areas and bulk-handling space around the bay. Island ferries run from the town to the Šibenik archipelago, and tour operators run excursions to the Kornati islands and the Krka waterfalls, so a considerable part of the local fleet is passenger vessels of moderate size. These operators schedule most of their work in summer and refit in winter.

Because the bay is deep, calm and removed from the main shipping lanes, ships sometimes wait here for charter orders or lay up between employment. That makes Šibenik unusual among smaller Croatian ports: a vessel may be idle for days or weeks, and an owner can use the time to gauge the structure thoroughly. The tidal range is small and currents in the channel are modest, although strong bora winds can arrive suddenly from the interior and make open-water launch transfers unwise. Fog is occasional in winter, and the channel's single approach means that pilotage and tug arrangements are always settled with the agent in advance.

facilities.h: Where gauging is practical in Šibenik
p: Šibenik does not offer the dry-dock infrastructure of a large repair port, and we do not assume any yard capacity unless the owner and the agent confirm it. What it does offer is time and calm water. A ship at a commercial quay after discharge can have holds, hatch covers and tank tops gauged in a normal working shift, while a vessel lying at a lay-by berth or at anchor in the inner bay may be available for several days, which allows a staged programme through ballast tanks, voids and deck structure.

Ferries and excursion vessels are usually gauged alongside at the town quays during winter, when schedules are light and crews have time to prepare tanks. Where a docking survey is needed, the ship normally proceeds to a yard elsewhere on the Adriatic, and gauging in Šibenik beforehand helps the yard plan steel work. The agent arranges quay access and passes, books launches for ships at anchor and coordinates tug or pilot movements if the ship needs to shift berth during the programme.
list: Commercial quays — holds, hatch covers, coamings and tank tops on general cargo and bulk ships after discharge
Lay-by berths in the inner bay — multi-day condition programmes on ships idle between charters
Anchorage in the inner harbour — launch access for pre-purchase, on-hire and off-hire gauging
Town ferry quays — island ferries gauged on vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks in winter lay-up
Excursion boat berths — hull and deck gauging on tour vessels before the summer season opens
Pre-docking visits — measured steel estimates for vessels about to sail for a yard elsewhere

context.h: Regulation and the Šibenik shipping scene
p: Foreign ships calling at Šibenik are covered by Paris MoU port state control, carried out by Croatian inspectors under the authority of the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure and the harbour master's authority for the Šibenik area. Smaller ships on short Adriatic runs get inspected less often than deep-sea traffic, but an old coaster with visible hatch cover wastage is an obvious target. Owners who plan to trade in the region for several more years often decide to gauge before an inspection, so that any deficiency can be fixed first.

The EU Ship Recycling Regulation and the EU emissions rules shape decisions here too. Larger ships must carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials when calling at EU ports, and ships above the size thresholds fall under EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. For the older coasters and ferries that make up much of the local fleet, those obligations are weighed against the measured condition of the steel. The Krka National Park and the Kornati islands bring heavy summer tourism, so tour vessels are a significant group: their operators care about both safety certificates and visible condition, and thickness readings support both.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Šibenik
jobs.p: Jobs in Šibenik are shaped by time and calm water. A coaster lying idle in the bay might need a full condition assessment before sale; a bulk carrier at a quay needs hold structure checked after discharge; a ferry in winter lay-up needs vehicle deck and tank readings before her docking elsewhere. We agree scope and report format with the superintendent before the team travels.
list: Pre-purchase gauging of an older coaster lying at a lay-by berth: main deck, hatch covers, ballast tanks and accessible hold structure
Hold and hatch cover gauging on a bulk carrier after discharge at a commercial quay, ahead of an intermediate survey
Winter lay-up programme on an island ferry at the town quay, covering vehicle deck, ramp hinges, voids and ballast tanks
Steel estimate for an excursion vessel before she sails to a yard, with readings on hull plating, decks and engine room tank tops
Off-hire condition check on a ship at anchor in the inner bay, recording measured values for the owner's records

logistics: Split Airport is the nearest large airport and lies within road distance, while Zadar Airport and Zagreb are also options. The ship's agent arranges quay passes and port access, and books launches for ships at anchor in the bay. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, so the visa schedule sets the earliest start. Longer lay-up programmes leave comfortable time for planning, whereas a short cargo call needs the berth and date confirmed as early as possible.
vessels: Ships laid up or waiting for orders

faqs.q: Is Šibenik a good place to gauge a ship that is laid up?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The inner bay is sheltered and quiet, so a vessel between charters can lie at a berth or at anchor for days. That gives time to gauge decks, tanks and holds in stages and to record readings carefully, which is harder to do on a short cargo call.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Šibenik?
faqs.a: We do not assume one. Dock availability should be confirmed with the owner and the agent. If a docking survey is needed, the ship normally goes to a yard elsewhere on the Adriatic, and we gauge in Šibenik beforehand so that the yard has a realistic steel estimate.

faqs.q: Can tour boats and ferries be gauged before the summer season?
faqs.a: Yes. Winter and early spring are the best times, when schedules are light and crews can prepare tanks. We measure hull, decks and tank boundaries, record the readings by location, and give the operator a clear view of what needs renewal before the season starts.

faqs.q: Does the channel affect work on ships at anchor?
faqs.a: Slightly. The channel is sheltered, but a bora wind can make launch transfers unsafe for a day. Pilotage rules also limit when a ship can shift berth, so we keep the plan flexible and agree the sequence with the agent before the team travels.
